title: WODCraft — the language of WODs
meta[name=description]@content: WODCraft: write a WOD the way it goes on the whiteboard; a compiler checks it and turns it into JSON for timers, apps and AI agents.
meta[property='og:description']@content: Write a WOD the way it goes on the whiteboard. A compiler reads it back.

.lede: WODCraft is a small language for prescribing functional-fitness workouts — and the compiler that checks them. Strict where it matters (units, movements, score coherence, plausibility), forgiving where coaches need it.
.why article:nth-child(1) p: Any valid file can be put on the wall of the box as is. No braces, no YAML: whiteboard syntax.
.why article:nth-child(2) p: A box jump takes a height, not a load. 1 m Run asks whether you meant 1 mi. An EMOM nobody can finish is flagged.
.why article:nth-child(3) p: The compiled JSON follows a versioned schema: it is what timers, apps and AI agents exchange.
.why article:nth-child(4) p: Loads carry kilos and pounds, with the equivalences boxes actually use: 95 lb ↔ 43 kg, 24 in ↔ 60 cm.
#how .sec-head p: Text goes in, a structured document comes out. Click a stage to see what it really produces for Fran.
#diag .sec-head p: Every diagnostic carries a code from the specification, an exact line and column — and a suggestion when there is one. Real output of wodc check.
#formats .sec-head p: For time, AMRAP, EMOM, intervals, Tabata, Death by, strength sets, teams, there and back… On the left what the coach writes, on the right what the board shows.
#profile .sec-head p: The coach writes Thruster 95/65 lb once. The compiler resolves it for each athlete: category, level, units, language.
#session .sec-head p: The real session of 29 September: warm-up, AMRAP, team chipper, core work. wodc timer turns it into the timer's run sheet.
#try h2: Try it — the real compiler, in your browser
#try .sec-head p: No server: WODCraft's Python package runs right here thanks to Pyodide. Edit the WOD, break it, compile.
#playOut: Press “Compile”: the compiler (≈ 10 MB with Python) loads the first time.
.everywhere .sec-head p: One specification, one schema, one conformance suite — and two implementations that check each other.
.cards article:nth-child(1) p: Check, display, format like gofmt, export to your calendar.
.cards article:nth-child(2) p: Language server and VS Code extension: live diagnostics, movement completion, hover, quick fixes.
.cards article:nth-child(3) p: An MCP server exposes the compiler itself. The agent drafts a WOD, the compiler answers, the agent fixes it.
.cards article:nth-child(4) p: WODCraftKit: the language ported to Swift, offline, validated by the same conformance suite.
.cards article:nth-child(5) p: For clients that cannot embed the compiler. Docker image ready for Cloud Run.
.cards article:nth-child(6) p: Specification (CC BY-SA), versioned JSON Schema and conformance cases: WODCraft is meant to be reimplemented.
